title: A/C System Check & Cooling Coach
subtitle: Cabin filter, visual checks, and knowing when refrigerant is a pro job — cool air without risky shortcuts.

prerequisites: Park level; engine bay cool enough to inspect safely
Correct cabin filter part for year/make/model
Do not vent refrigerant to atmosphere
tools_checklist: Screwdrivers / trim tools for cabin filter
parts_checklist: Do NOT rely on DIY recharge cans as a fix

adaptive_rules.coach_note: Hot climates work the A/C hard — clogged cabin filters and low refrigerant show up as weak center vents by mid-afternoon.
Many EVs use heat pumps. Weird climate behavior may be software/thermal strategy — still start with filter and cabin settings before parts.
Tesla: check cabin filter service intervals in the manual; refrigerant and heat-pump diagnostics are service-center work.
European cars often hide cabin filters under glovebox panels — follow torque/clips carefully.
Past 100k, weak A/C often means leak + recharge by a shop with leak test — not repeated DIY cans.
